en: The Section on Further Exposition, Chapter Eleven: Convergence (Sampāta)
The Convergence of the Mode of Conveying Description.
Therein, what is the convergence of the mode of conveying description?
It is the verse: “Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, the range is right intention.”
“Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded”: this is a designation of the proximate cause (*padaṭṭhāna-paññatti*) for mindfulness.
“Having right intention as his range”: this is a designation of development (*bhāvanā-paññatti*) for serenity (*samatha*).

“Having right view as his priority, knowing arising and passing away”: this is a designation of the laying down [of the teaching] (*nikkhepa-paññatti*) regarding the plane of vision (*dassana-bhūmi*).

“A bhikkhu overcome by sloth and torpor”: this is a description of the abandoning of the origin [of suffering] without remainder. “He should abandon all miserable destinies”: this is a description of the path as a state of cultivation.
The section on the Modes of Conveying Descriptions is concluded.
